(a) Definitions. For purpose of this section, the following definitions shall apply:
Highway: Defined as in O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1(19), which is incorporated by reference as if fully set forth in this section.
Noise: Any sound that is excessive in volume, frequency or duration as would disrupt the peace and quiet reasonable people with ordinary sensibilities. Sounds that are plainly audible to a person of normal hearing ability from the distance of 50 feet from the point of origin shall be presumed to be "noise" in violation of this section.
Private property: Any dwelling, house, building or other structure, whether inhabited or used permanently or temporarily or continuously uninhabited or vacant and which is 100 percent privately owned and shall include any real property, yard, grounds, walk, parking area, driveway, porch, steps, vestibule or any portion or addition thereof belonging or pertinent to such dwelling, house, building or structure or any land, area or lot that does not have an existing structure within the boundaries of the property.
Public place means any area that is used or held out for use by the public, whether owned or operated by public or private interests, including but not limited to streets, parking lots parking garages, sidewalks, rights-of-way, parks, campgrounds, highways, alleys and other public ways.
(b) Prohibited noise. No person shall yell, shout, sing, chant, or make any other loud or raucous noises by any means whatsoever, whether by voice, hand-clapping, stomping or mechanical means, in a manner which constitutes "noise" as defined in this section. This section and its prohibitions shall apply equally to noise that originates and/or is heard on public property, private property (whether it be office, commercial, industrial, agricultural, or residential), and on the highways of the county or in proximity thereto. Such sounds which are audible to a person with normal hearing ability from the distance of 50 feet from the point of origin are presumed to be "noise" in violation of this section.
For purposes of this section, such mechanical sound includes, but is not limited to, the usage of firearms or pyrotechnics, the production of sound caused by the construction, destruction, or maintenance of any building, dwelling or structure, the building or maintenance of any mechanical contrivance, including motor vehicles, common lawn equipment and agricultural machinery, or the operation of any mechanical device.
The following acts among others are declared to be per se in violation of this section, but this enumeration shall not be deemed to be exclusive:
(1) Horns, signaling devices. The sounding of any horn or signaling device on any automobile, motorcycle or other vehicle on any street or public place in the county, except as a danger warning; the creation of any unreasonably loud or harsh sound by means of this signaling device and the sounding of this device for an unreasonable period of time; the use of any signaling device, except one operated by hand or electricity; the use of any horn, whistle or other device operated by engine exhaust and the use of this signaling device when traffic is for any reason held up is prohibited.
(2) Radios, phonographs, similar devices. The using, operating or permitting to be played, used or operated of any radio receiving set, musical instrument, phonograph or other machine or device for the producing or reproducing of sound in such manner as to unreasonably disturb the peace, quiet, repose of reasonable persons of ordinary sensibilities or at any time with louder volume than is reasonably necessary for convenient hearing for the person who is in the room, vehicle or chamber in which this machine or device is operated and who is a voluntary listener thereto. The operation of the set, instrument, phonograph machine or device between the hours of 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. in such a manner as to be plainly audible at a distance of 50 feet from the origin of sound produced shall be presumed to be a violation of this section.
(3) Loudspeakers, amplifiers for advertising. The using, operating or permitting to be played, used, or operated of any radio receiving set, musical instrument, phonograph, loudspeaker, sound amplifier or other device for producing or reproducing sound which is cast upon the public streets for the purpose of commercial advertising or attracting the attention of the public to any building or structure is prohibited. Such announcements over loudspeakers shall only be made by the announcer in person and without the aid of any mechanical device.
(4) Yelling, shouting and the like. Yelling, shouting, hooting whistling or singing, particularly between the hours of 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. or at any time or place so as to unreasonably disturb the quiet, comfort or repose of reasonable persons of ordinary sensibilities is prohibited. Such noise that is plainly audible at a distance of 50 feet from the origin of sound shall be presumed to be in violation of this section.
(5) Noisy animals or birds. Anyone who keeps or maintains an animal or bird that unreasonably disturbs the comfort or repose of any reasonable person with ordinary sensibilities, because the animal or bird is emitting frequent or long continued sound or noise, and who continues to keep, maintain, or allow any animal or bird to so disturb the comfort or repose of any reasonable person with ordinary sensibilities shall be deemed in violation of this section, provided that the person keeping or maintaining the animal or bird has been first notified in writing by certified mail, return receipt requested, by the complaining party that this animal or bird being kept by the addressee is unreasonably disturbing his or her comfort or repose. This section shall be liberally construed to accomplish the objective of the section, and the person making this written notification need not use the exact words of this section to the addressee so long as the notification sufficiently informs the addressee of the nature of the disturbing noise emitted by the animal or bird. Upon receipt of a certified letter notifying the person keeping or maintaining such animal or bird, such person shall be required to immediately comply with this section. This section shall not apply to horses, livestock, poultry or other farm animals, provided the sound is emanating from a legitimate farming operation on property that is properly zoned for such use.
(6) Construction or repair of buildings. The erection, excavating, demolition, alteration or repair of any building other than between the hours of 7:00 a.m. to 11 p.m. on weekdays shall be prohibited, except when the Barrow County Building Inspector deems on-site situation warrants an extended time. The Barrow County Building Inspector may grant a special permit extending this time which is not to exceed ten working days for this work to be done between the hours of 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m.
(7) Transportation of metal rails, similar materials. The transportation of rails, pillars or columns of iron, steel or other material over and along streets and other public places upon carts, drays, cars, trucks or in any manner so loaded as to cause unreasonably loud noises or as to unreasonably disturb the peace and quiet of reasonable persons with ordinary sensibilities is prohibited.
(8) Pile drivers, hammers, and similar equipment. The operation between the hours of 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. of this type tool shall be prohibited. Included in this category, but not limited to, is steam shovel, pneumatic hammers derricks, steam or electric hoist, fork lifts and the like.
(9) Blowers and motors. The operation of any noise-creating blower or power fan or any internal combustion engine, the operation of which causes noises due to explosion of operating gases or fluids is prohibited, unless the noise from this blower or fan is muffled and the engine is equipped with a muffler device specifically designed for the type engine and is not adapted, altered or make-shift and provides reasonable sufficiency in muffling the engine noise.
(10) Sound trucks. The use of sound trucks for noncommercial purposes with such unreasonable volume as to disturb the peace and quiet of reasonable persons with ordinary sensibilities is prohibited. Such sound that is plainly audible at a distance of 50 feet from the origin of sound shall be presumed to be a violation of this section.
(11) Steam whistles. Any steam whistle attached to a stationary boiler is prohibited, except to give notice of the time to begin or stop work or as a warning of fire or danger upon request of proper authorities.
(12) Exhausts. The discharge into the open air of the exhaust of any steam engine, stationary internal combustion engine or motor vehicle or boat is prohibited, except through a muffler which is specifically designed for the type engine and is not adapted, altered or make-shift, providing reasonable sufficiency in muffling engine noise.
a. All engines for the purpose of racing, be it car, motorcycle, truck or go-cart shall be equipped with approved racing mufflers and shall cease operation on Monday through Friday between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. and shall further cease operations on Saturday and Sunday between the hours of 11:30 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. Moreover, the operators and owners of any racing facility shall be responsible for racing participants being in compliance with muffler usage and the other provisions of this section and shall be subject to enforcement under this section for failure to so control racing participants.
(13) Defect in vehicle or load. The use of any automobile, motorcycle or vehicle so out of repair, so loaded or in such manner as to create unreasonably loud and unnecessary grating, grinding, ratting or other noises so as to disturb the peace and quiet of reasonable persons with ordinary sensibilities are prohibited. Such sound that is plainly audible at a distance of 50 feet from the origin of sound shall be presumed to be a violation of this section.
(14) Schools, courts, churches, hospitals. The creation of any unreasonably excessive noise on any street adjacent to any school, institution of learning, church or court while the same are in use, or adjacent to any hospital, which unreasonably interferes with the normal operation of the institution, or which disturbs reasonable persons with ordinary sensibilities is prohibited, provided that conspicuous signs are displayed in the streets indicating that is a school, hospital or court street. Sound that is plainly audible inside the institution shall be presumed to be a violation of this section.
(15) Hawkers, peddlers, vendors. The shouting and crying of peddlers, hawkers and vendors which disturbs the peace and quiet of reasonable persons with ordinary sensibilities is prohibited. Such sound that is plainly audible at a distance of 50 feet from the origin of sound shall be presumed to be a violation of this section.
(16) Noises to attract attention. The use of any drum or other instrument or device for the purpose of attracting attention to any performance, show car sale, or the like so as to disturb reasonable persons with ordinary sensibilities is prohibited. Such sound that is plainly audible at a distance of 50 feet from the origin of sound shall be presumed to be a violation of this section.
(17) Operation of motor vehicles. The operation of motor vehicles, including, but not limited to, cars, trucks, motorcycles, all-terrain vehicles, and mopeds, upon any parking facility, public or private, vehicle access or pedestrian walkway, or street, public or private, so as to create unreasonable noise and to disturb the peace, quiet and repose of reasonable persons with ordinary sensibilities is prohibited. Such sound that is plainly audible at a distance of 50 feet from the origin of sound shall be presumed to be a violation of this section. The operation of motor vehicles which employ Jakebrakes that are used in a manner to cause unnecessary noise is prohibited.
(c) Exceptions. The provisions of this section shall not apply to or be enforced against:
(1) Any vehicle of the county while engaged in necessary public business.
(2) Excavations or repairs of streets by or on behalf of the county or state at night when public welfare and convenience renders it impossible to perform this work during the day.
(3) Organized school-related programs, activities, events or parades or other public programs, activities or events authorized by the county or sheriff's office.
(4) Noise resulting from emergency work, to be construed to mean work made necessary to restore property to a safe condition following a public calamity, or work required to protect persons or property from imminent exposure to danger.
(5) Noise emanating from approved construction sites associated with reasonable construction activities, provided that the noise occurs only during daylight hours and does not disturb reasonable persons of ordinary sensibilities who are nearby residents.
(6) Noise emanating from commercial, industrial, or manufacturing districts, provided that the noise occurs only during daylight hours and does not disturb reasonable persons of ordinary sensibilities and the business producing such noises are properly permitted.
(7) Noise associated with hunting activities, provided that the hunting activities are occurring on land properly zoned for such activities and provided that all activities are in conformance with applicable law.
(d) Special variances:
(1) The board of commissioners shall have the authority, consistent with this section, to grant variances.
(2) Any person seeking a variance pursuant to this section shall file an application with the director of license and permits (the "director"). The application shall contain information that demonstrates that bringing the source of sound into compliance with this section would constitute an unreasonable hardship on the applicant, on the community, or on other persons. The director shall give notice of an application for a special variance to persons who frequent the area of the sound or activity and who may be adversely affected by the granting of the variance by posting the property and by letter to adjoining property owners. Any individual who claims to be adversely affected by allowances of the variance may file a statement with the director within ten days of receiving notice of the special variance request, which statement should contain any information to support such individual's claim. The director shall forward the application and any responsive statements to the board of commissioners for its consideration.
(3) In determining whether to grant or deny the application, the board of commissioners shall balance the hardship to the applicant, the community, and other persons of not granting the special variance against the adverse impact on the health, safety, and welfare of other persons affected by the granting of the special variance. The variance request will also be otherwise considered by the board of commissioners under the variance standards set forth in the Barrow County Zoning and Development Regulations, which regulations are incorporated herein by reference as if fully set forth herein.
(4) Applicants for special variances may be required to submit any information the board of commissioners may reasonably require for its consideration of the request.
(5) In granting or denying an application, the board of commissioners shall place on public file, a copy of the decision and reasons for denying or granting the special variance.
(6) Special variances shall be granted by notice to the applicant containing all necessary conditions, including a time limit on the permitted activity. The special variance shall not become effective until the applicant agrees to all conditions. Noncompliance with any condition of the special variance shall terminate the special variance and subject the person holding it to those provisions of this section regulating the source of sound or activity for which the special variance was granted.
(7) Application for extension of time limits specified in special variances or for modification of other substantial conditions shall be treated like applications for initial special variances.
(8) Enforcement of this article shall be stayed as to any person filing an application for a special variance pursuant to this section, until such time as the board of commissioners acts upon the application.
(9) The decision of the board of commissioners is final.
(10) Special events, including but not limited to carnivals, fairs, tent meetings, revivals, rallies, festivals, concerts or any public gathering, whether for the purpose of disseminating information, entertainment or political speech, must have a special variance to be exempted from this section.
(e) Enforcement; penalty.
(1) This section shall be enforceable by all law enforcement personnel duly ordained and empowered to enforce the laws and ordinances in the county. If a violation is construed as a moving traffic violation, the Barrow County Sheriff's Office shall be responsible for enforcement and shall be responsible for enforcement when responding to a complaint or when a vehicle in violation may be tracked through use of a tag search and cited for the violation at a fixed location.
(2) Any person found in violation of any of the provisions of this section shall be found guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be subject to a fine of not less than $250.00 and not more than $1,000.00 or be imprisoned in the county jail or correctional institution for a period not to exceed 60 days or both, for each offense for which the offender is convicted.
(3) For purposes of this section, each day that a violation is committed or permitted shall be punishable as a separate offense. In addition, each subsequent occasion on which a law enforcement officer must respond to the same incident after an initial citation is written shall be considered a separate offense, regardless of whether the later responses occur on the same day as the first citation.
(f) Jurisdiction of magistrate court. The Magistrate Court of Barrow County shall have jurisdiction to try the offenses described in this section.

472:
For purposes of this resolution, the following definitions apply:
'County' means Barrow County, Georgia.
'Covered account' means: (i) an account that a financial institution or creditor offers or maintains, primarily for personal, family, or household purposes, that involves or is designed to permit multiple payments or transactions, such as a credit card account, mortgage loan, automobile loan, margin account, cell phone account, utility account, checking account, or savings account; and (ii) any other account that the financial institution or creditor offers or maintains for which there is a reasonably foreseeable risk to customers or to the safety and soundness of the financial institution or creditor from identity theft, including financial, operational, compliance, reputation, or litigation risks.
'Credit' means the right granted by a creditor to a debtor to defer payment of debt or to incur debts and defer its payment or to purchase property or services and defer payment therefore.
'Creditor' means any person who regularly extends, renews, or continues credit; any person who regularly arranges for the extension, renewal, or continuation of credit; or any assignee of an original creditor who participates in the decision to extend, renew, or continue credit and includes utility companies and telecommunications companies.
'Customer' means a person who has a covered account with the county.
'Identity theft' means a fraud committed or attempted using identifying information of another person without authority.
'Person' means a natural person, a corporation, government or governmental subdivision or agency, trust, estate, partnership, cooperative, or association.
'Personal identifying information' means a person's credit card account information, debit card information bank account information and drivers' license information and for a natural person includes their social security number, mother's birth name, and date of birth.
'Program' shall mean the Identity Theft Prevention Program implemented by this resolution.
'Red flag' means a pattern, practice, or specific activity that indicates the possible existence of identity theft.
'Service provider' means a person that provides a service directly to the county.
(Res. of 4-28-2009, § 1.3)
473:
(a) The county is a creditor pursuant to 16 CFR § 681.2 due to its provision or maintenance of covered accounts for which payment is made in arrears.
(b) Covered accounts offered to customers for the provision of county services are limited to water/sewer services.
(c) The county is aware of previous suspected instances of potential identity theft related to covered accounts.
(d) The processes of opening a new covered account, restoring an existing covered account, making payments on such accounts have been identified as potential processes in which identity theft could occur.
(e) The county limits access to personal identifying information to those employees responsible for or otherwise involved in opening or restoring covered accounts or accepting payment for use of covered accounts. Beginning no later than January 1, 2010, information provided to such employees will be entered directly into the county's computer system and will not be otherwise recorded.
(f) The county determines that there is a risk of identity theft occurring in the following ways:
(1) Use by an applicant of another person's personal identifying information to establish a new covered account;
(2) Use of a previous customer's personal identifying information by another person in an effort to have service restored in the previous customer's name;
(3) Use of another person's credit card, bank account, or other method of payment by a customer to pay such customer's covered account or accounts;
(4) Use by a customer desiring to restore such customer's covered account of another person's credit card, bank account, or other method of payment.
(Res. of 4-28-2009, § 1.4)
474:
(a) As a precondition to opening a covered account in the county, county personnel will take reasonable steps including but not limited to the following to obtain and verify the identity of the person opening the account:

(2) Verify the customer's identity by reviewing documentation provided.

477:
All employees responsible for or involved in the process of opening a covered account, restoring a covered account or accepting payment for a covered account shall check for red flags as indicators of possible identity theft and such red flags may include:
(1) Alerts from consumer reporting agencies, fraud detection agencies or service providers. Examples of alerts include but are not limited to:
a. A fraud or active duty alert that is included with a consumer report;
b. A notice of credit freeze in response to a request for a consumer report;
c. A notice of address discrepancy provided by a consumer reporting agency;
d. Indications of a pattern of activity in a consumer report that is inconsistent with the history and usual pattern of activity of an applicant or customer, such as:
i. A recent and significant increase in the volume of inquiries;
ii. An unusual number of recently established credit relationships;
iii. A material change in the use of credit, especially with respect to recently established credit relationships; or
iv. An account that was closed for cause or identified for abuse of account privileges by a financial institution or creditor.
(2) Suspicious documents. Examples of suspicious documents include:
a. Documents provided for identification that appear to be altered or forged;
b. Identification on which the photograph or physical description is inconsistent with the appearance of the applicant or customer;
c. Identification on which the information is inconsistent with information provided by the applicant or customer;
d. Identification on which the information is inconsistent with readily accessible information that is on file with the county, such as a signature card or a recent check; or
e. An application that appears to have been altered or forged, or appears to have been destroyed and reassembled.
(3) Suspicious personal identification, such as a suspicious address change. Examples of suspicious identifying information include:
a. Personal identifying information that is inconsistent with external information sources used by the county. For example:
i. The address does not match any address in any available consumer report; or
ii. The Social Security Number ("SSN") has not been issued, or is listed on the Social Security Administration's Death Master File.
b. Personal identifying information provided by the customer is not consistent with other personal identifying information provided by the customer, such as a lack of correlation between the SSN range and date of birth.
c. Personal identifying information or a phone number or address, is associated with known fraudulent applications or activities as indicated by internal or third-party sources used by the county.
d. Other information provided, such as fictitious mailing address, mail drop addresses, jail addresses, invalid phone numbers, pager numbers or answering services, is associated with fraudulent activity.
e. The SSN provided is the same as that submitted by other applicants or customers.
f. The address or telephone number provided is the same as or similar to the account number or telephone number submitted by an unusually large number of applicants or customers.
g. The applicant or customer fails to provide all required personal identifying information on an application or in response to notification that the application is incomplete.
h. Personal identifying information is not consistent with personal identifying information that is on file with the county.
i. The applicant or customer cannot provide authenticating information beyond that which generally would be available from a wallet or consumer report.
(4) Unusual use of or suspicious activity relating to a covered account. Examples of suspicious activity include:
a. Shortly following the notice of a change of address for an account, county receives a request for the addition of authorized users on the account.
b. A new revolving credit account is used in a manner commonly associated with known patterns of fraud. For example, the customer fails to make the first payment or makes an initial payment but no subsequent payments.
c. An account is used in a manner that is not consistent with established patterns of activity on the account. There is, for example:
i. Nonpayment when there is no history of late or missed payments;
ii. A material change in purchasing or spending patterns;
d. An account that has been inactive for a long period of time is used (taking into consideration the type of account, the expected pattern of usage and other relevant factors).
e. Mail sent to the customer is returned repeatedly as undeliverable although transactions continue to be conducted in connection with the customer's account.
f. The county is notified that the customer is not receiving paper account statements.
g. The county is notified of unauthorized charges or transactions in connection with a customer's account.
h. The county is notified by a customer, law enforcement or another person that it has opened a fraudulent account for a person engaged in identity theft.
(5) Notice from customers, law enforcement, victims or other reliable sources regarding possible identity theft or "phishing" relating to covered accounts.
(Res. of 4-28-2009, § 1.8)

502:

503:

(Res. of 2-11-1997, § 5(3))
504:

505:

(Res. of 2-11-1997, § 9)
508:

(Res. of 2-11-1997, § 4(1))
509:
The officers of the parks and recreation board shall be chairperson, vice-chairperson, secretary and treasurer. These officers shall be elected from the parks and recreation board members by a majority vote of the parks and recreation board members present and voting.
(Res. of 2-11-1997, § 7)
510:
The officers of the parks and recreation board shall be elected by secret ballot annually, and shall serve for the term of one-year, not to exceed two consecutive terms.
(Res. of 2-11-1997, § 7)
511:
The chairperson of the parks and recreation board shall be responsible for presiding at all parks and recreation board meetings; shall serve as parks and recreation board liaison between the parks and recreation board and the board of commissioners and other funding agencies; shall be spokesperson for the parks and recreation board voicing those policies of the parks and recreation board which have been determined by a majority vote of the parks and recreation board; shall appoint such standing committees or temporary committees as the chairperson deems necessary to the efficient operation of the business of the parks and recreation board; shall be responsible for making an annual report on the parks and recreation board to the board of commissioners. The director and other officers of the parks and recreation board shall assist the chairperson in compiling this report which shall cover financial as well as activities of the recreation program.
(Res. of 2-11-1997, § 7)
512:
The vice-chairperson shall preside at any meetings from which the chairperson must be absent; shall assist the chairperson in any of the chairperson's duties, where necessary; shall be responsible for taking an interested oversight in the general activities of the recreation program; and shall assist the director in an advisory capacity, wherever needed and/or requested in improving activities already in the program or in adding new activity areas to the existing program. The vice-chairperson shall become the chairperson, should that office become vacant by resignation or otherwise.
(Res. of 2-11-1997, § 7)
513:
The parks and recreation board shall appoint a secretary who may be an officer or employee of the county, or of the parks and recreation board. The secretary shall be responsible for taking the minutes of each parks and recreation board meeting; shall assist the chairperson in compiling the annual report (a copy of which shall be attached to that year's minutes as a permanent reference); and perform such other functions as may be required of the secretary.
(Res. of 2-11-1997, §§ 4(2), 7)
514:
The treasurer shall receive all monies for the parks and recreation board and deposit all monies in such depositories as the parks and recreation board may direct; shall pay all bills and charges approved by the parks and recreation board; shall render to the parks and recreation board a financial statement at such intervals as the parks and recreation board may direct; shall itemize the expenses and income for the period reported; and shall attend to such other duties as may be assigned by the chairperson.
(Res. of 2-11-1997, § 7)
515:
(a) The board of commissioners shall appoint a recreation director and such other staff and employees as it may deem necessary to properly and adequately conduct the recreation program. However, the salaries of such officers and employees shall be within and consistent with the budget established and approved. All such personnel shall be subject to the personnel plan of the county.
(b) The duties of the director shall be to plan, organize, direct and control a countywide recreation program, pursuant to the policy established by the board of commissioners and within the budget submitted to and approved by the county's governing bodies. The director shall report all progress on activities to the parks and recreation board as requested by the board of commissioners. Checks issued by the parks and recreation board shall require the signature of the director and the chairperson of the parks and recreation board.
(Res. of 2-11-1997, § 6)
518:
The parks and recreation board shall hold regular bimonthly meetings at a time and place to be designated by the parks and recreation board.
(Res. of 2-11-1997, § 8A)
519:
Special meetings of the parks and recreation board may be called by the chairperson at the request of three members of the parks and recreation board.
(Res. of 2-11-1997, § 8B)
520:
A quorum of the parks and recreation board shall consist of four members for any meeting of the parks and recreation board.
(Res. of 2-11-1997, § 8C)
521:
Minutes of all meetings of the parks and recreation board shall be taken to reflect an accurate reporting of the business conducted. These minutes shall be available to all persons and organizations upon request.
(Res. of 2-11-1997, § 8D)
522:
The annual meeting of the parks and recreation board shall be held at the September meeting each year. At this meeting the officers shall be elected for the coming year.
(Res. of 2-11-1997, § 8E)
523:
The parks and recreation board shall make its own rules of procedure, consistent with state law and the authority granted it by resolution of the county. Generally, the procedure at meetings of the parks and recreation board shall be governed by the latest edition of Robert's Rules of Order, Newly Revised.
(Res. of 2-11-1997, §§ 4(3), 10)

(a) Prior to initiating any formal annexation activities, the city will notify the county planning department in writing by certified mail, return receipt requested of a proposed annexation and provide information on location of property, size of area and proposed land use and zoning classifications of the property upon annexation. Within 30 working days following receipt of the above information, the county will forward to the city in writing by certified mail, return receipt requested, a statement either:
(1) Indicating that the county has no objections to the proposed land use for the property; or
(2) Describing its bona fide objections to the city's proposed land use classification, providing supporting information, and listing any possible stipulations or conditions that would alleviate the county's objections.
(b) If the county has no objection to the city's proposed land use and zoning classification, the city is free to proceed with the annexation. If the county fails to respond to the city's notice in writing within the allotted time, the city is free to proceed with the annexation and the county loses its right to invoke the dispute resolution process, stop the annexation or object to land use changes after the annexation.
(c) If the county notifies the city that it has bona fide land use classification objections, the city will respond to the county in writing by certified mail, return receipt requested, within 30 working days of receiving the county's objections by either:
(1) Agreeing to implement the county's stipulations and conditions and thereby resolving the county's objections;
(2) Agreeing with the county and stopping the action on the proposed annexation;
(3) Disagreeing that the county's objections are bona fide and notifying the county that the city will seek a declaratory judgment in court; or
(4) Initiating a 30-day maximum mediation process to discuss possible compromises.
(d) If the city initiates mediation, the Northeast Georgia Regional Development Center shall assist the city and the county in the selection of a mediator acceptable to both parties. After acceptance of a mediator, the city and county shall agree on a mediation schedule and appoint representatives to participate in the mediation process. The cost for mediation shall be borne equally by the city and the county.
(e) If no resolution of the county's bona fide land use classification objections results from the mediation, the city will not proceed with the proposed annexation.
(f) If the city and county reach agreement as described in subsection (c)(1) or as a result of the mediation, they will draft an annexation agreement for execution by the city and the county government and the property owners.
(g) Regardless of future changes in land use or zoning classification, any site-specific mitigation or enhancement measures or site-design stipulations included in the agreement will be binding on all parties for duration of the annexation agreement. The agreement shall become final when signed by the city, the county and the property owners.
(Res. of 7-1-1998)
